resource_metric: l2_gas (sierra gas); l1_gas=0 and l1_data_gas=0 for all tests

baseline.description: O(n²) linear-scan + full array rebuild per insertion (original ve.cairo)
baseline.accumulate_cost: O(n) copies per insertion, O(n²) total for n entries

dict.description: Felt252Dict<u128> with separate key_list + is_new dict (ve_dict.cairo)
dict.accumulate_cost: O(1) amortized insert + O(k log k) squash at drop
dict.count_type: u128 (truncated; sufficient for chain fixtures, not 471-bit corpus)
dict.limitation: squash overhead dominates for small tables

findings.winner_rationale: Felt252Dict squash overhead (~O(k log k)) outweighs O(1) insert savings for small sparse tables (nonzero entries ≤ 103). Dict is consistently 2.1-2.2× more expensive across all fixtures.
findings.key_insight: For VE with small factors (max 103 nonzero entries, max 7 variables), the O(n²) linear scan has low enough constant factor that dict overhead dominates.

baseline_scale.note: Sub-quadratic growth from f3→f6→f7 suggests join count and treewidth dominate, not accumulate size

dict_scale.note: Similar growth pattern — squash cost scales similarly to linear scan for these table sizes

findings.next_bottleneck: Not accumulate overhead but total join count and treewidth. For real corpus cases (23-26 vars, treewidth up to 6), the factor sizes grow exponentially. Real CELL query cost: estimated 30-100M+ gas/evaluation.
findings.dense_array_status: Discarded before implementation: 39,680 slot initialization cost in Cairo exceeds accumulate savings for corpus-scale (103 nonzero / 39,680 slots = 0.26% occupancy)

state_key_ranges.mines_used: 0..30 (NOT bounded by scope_len; accumulates ALL eliminated vars)
